stories.primary_headline: Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede

primary_source.headline: Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede
primary_source.content: The stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata claimed the lives of 19 people, while 25 others were injured. A senior police officer told PTI that lack of crowd management and misleading announcements following sudden heavy rainfall during Saptami celebrations could have led to the tragic incident. Police also found that the number of police personnel and private security guards deployed at the venue was inadequate, worsening the situation."We have gathered sufficient evidence pointing to gross mismanagement by the puja organisers. There was no clear plan to manage the large number of visitors, and everything was handled verbally. We have collected CCTV camera footage, recorded accounts from locals and eyewitnesses, and corroborated our findings. Security personnel were inadequate," the police officer told PTI.At least 19 dead, 25 others injured in stampede-like situation at Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata"Due to the mismanagement, people tried to escape through the entrance gate during the stampede. Both the gates and the approach road were narrow, which contributed to the accident," he said, adding that announcements regarding entry, exit and crowd movement were misleading, leaving visitors confused during the rush."We have video footage of an announcement asking people to leave the pandal on the grounds that the structure was about to collapse. We are trying to identify who made the announcement and what prompted it," the officer said.Moreover, the locals also claimed that police deployment was inadequate, alleging that personnel were mainly stationed near the VIP entrance.A team of forensic experts visited the pandal on Saturday night and collected evidence from the site, he said."Another team of forensic experts will visit the pandal today to collect further evidence. Officers from our Detective Department will also visit the venue as part of the investigation," he said.The Kolkata Police could question survivors as part of the probe, the IPS officer said."We need first-hand accounts to cross-check the findings based on statements from locals and other eyewitnesses. This will help our investigation," he added.Meanwhile, prohibitory orders under Section 163 have been imposed on roads adjoining the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Sunday morning.The order prohibits gatherings on roads surrounding the venue, which falls under the jurisdiction of Bowbazar Police Station. The restrictions will remain in force until October 20.Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that the state government would provide Rs 25 lakh in compensation and a Group D government job to the family of each deceased victim.He also ordered the formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court, to investigate the incident.

stories.primary_headline: Gwalior temple tragedy: MP CM orders removal of SP, suspension of 8 other police personnel

primary_source.headline: Gwalior temple tragedy: MP CM orders removal of SP, suspension of 8 other police personnel
primary_source.content: Bhopal: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday ordered the removal of the Gwalior City Superintendent of Police and the suspension of eight other personnel after the temple accident that claimed 14 lives when a truck ploughed into devotees.The speeding truck ran over several devotees outside the Sheetla Mata temple in Gwalior district early Sunday and then rammed into its entrance gate, killing 14 persons and injuring 28 others, including two police personnel, officials said. Seven of those injured were in critical condition.A wall of the temple crashed under the impact of the collision, they said.'Came like a storm': Eyewitnesses recall truck's deadly dash towards Gwalior templeThe incident, which occurred around 1.30 am outside the temple near a slope on Chinor Road, raised concerns about security arrangements at the shrine, as the truck, with a Punjab registration number, entered the no-entry zone, officials said."The accident occurred because the truck entered a prohibited area," Yadav told reporters in Indore.The chief minister said he had directed the district administration to conduct a fact-based inquiry and submit a report.Later, in a post on X, Yadav said his government has ordered the removal of the Gwalior CSP from his post and the suspension of three station house officers, a traffic inspector, a head constable and three constables.A detailed inquiry has been ordered to fix responsibility and ensure strict action against those found guilty, he said."The safety of all citizens is paramount. To prevent the recurrence of such incidents in future, security arrangements will be reviewed and necessary steps taken. No negligence will be tolerated at any level in public safety," he said.Yadav also announced compensation of Rs 4 lakh each for the kin of the deceased and said the government would bear the treatment expenses of those seriously injured in the accident. His family took the body away amid inconsolable grief. He had gone to the temple to offer prayers when the accident occurred.Sandeep, a relative of injured devotee Nikesh, said the family received a phone call around 5 am informing them that Nikesh had been hurt at the temple. When they reached the hospital, he was in critical condition with both legs fractured and was placed on a ventilator, he added.

stories.primary_headline: Pakistan extends airspace ban on Indian aircraft till November 24

primary_source.headline: Pakistan extends airspace ban on Indian aircraft till November 24
primary_source.content: Islamabad: Pakistan has extended its airspace ban on Indian-registered aircraft and planes owned, operated or leased by Indian airlines for another month, until November 24, according to the country's airports authority.The restriction, initially imposed on April 23, 2025, has been extended periodically since then amid strained relations between the two neighbouring countries.The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) announced the extension in a post on X on Saturday, saying the restriction also covers military flights.The latest extension will remain in effect until 4:59 am (local time) on November 24, 2026, according to the authority.Pakistan says it launched air strikes on Afghanistan over drone attacksA PAA spokesperson said a fresh Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued to extend the ban, Geo News reported.Pakistan’s airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs) -- Karachi and Lahore, according to a Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document from 2022. The latest NOTAM applies to both the Karachi and Lahore FIRs.India and Pakistan imposed reciprocal airspace restrictions on each other's aircraft following the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.India accused Pakistan of involvement in the attack, an allegation Islamabad denied. The incident was followed by a sharp escalation in diplomatic and military tensions between the two countries.India closed its airspace to Pakistani airlines on April 30, 2025, in response to Pakistan's move.Pakistan has imposed airspace restrictions on Indian aircraft during previous periods of heightened tensions, including the 1999 Kargil conflict and the 2019 Pulwama crisis, according to Geo News.The continuing airspace restrictions have affected airline operations between the two countries, forcing carriers to take longer routes on some international flights.

stories.primary_headline: Voters can fill Form 6 to get names re-included in electoral rolls: Election Commission to Delhi High Court

primary_source.headline: Voters can fill Form 6 to get names re-included in electoral rolls: Election Commission to Delhi High Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Election Commission of India has told the Delhi High Court that two voters, whose names were deleted from the electoral rolls after they could not complete the enumeration process during the Special Intensive Revision in the national capital, can fill Form 6 for redressal of their grievance.The statement was made on behalf of the Commission before the court, which was dealing with a petition seeking restoration of names of two petitioners in the electoral rolls.The court closed the plea noting that the petitioner's apprehension that if he fills Form 6, he would be accused of furnishing a false declaration was “misplaced”.From removing Form 6 declaration to capping Form 7 submissions: All changes EC made in last three weeks amid SIR row“Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, we are of the considered opinion that when the suggestion is coming from the learned standing counsel appearing for the ECI, that too as per the instructions of the electoral registration officer, petitioner No.1's apprehension that he would be accused of furnishing a false declaration is misplaced.“With these observations, the writ proceedings are closed. The petitioners, if so desire, may fill Form 6, which shall be processed in accordance with law,” a bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Aditi Choudhary said.The petitioners approached the court challenging the procedure prescribed by the ECI for the existing electors who could not be enumerated during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.They sought directions to restore their electoral entries and permit correction and transposition of their names through Form 8 instead of requiring them to seek fresh inclusion through Form 6.Their grievance was that they had shifted from their previous address and, consequently, could not fill the enumeration forms, resulting in the deletion of their names from the electoral rolls.The counsel for ECI submitted that the petitioners could get their grievance redressed by furnishing Form 6 under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.He also said that the electoral registration officer would extend assistance, but the petitioners have chosen not to do so for the reasons best known to them.Form 6 is the statutory application for fresh inclusion in the electoral roll. It requires an applicant to fill in their personal particulars.Applicants are also required to affirm that they are applying for inclusion in the electoral roll for the first time. Giving a false declaration can attract penal consequences.

stories.primary_headline: 'Came like a storm': Eyewitnesses recall truck's deadly dash towards Gwalior temple

primary_source.headline: 'Came like a storm': Eyewitnesses recall truck's deadly dash towards Gwalior temple
primary_source.content: Gwalior (MP): Screams shattered the stillness of the night as a speeding truck hurtled down a slope towards the Sheetla Mata temple in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior, crushing devotees waiting to catch a glimpse of the goddess and leaving behind a trail of devastation in the small hours of Sunday.Eyewitnesses described the Punjab-registered vehicle coming in "like a storm" through the no-entry zone near the shrine, triggering chaos within seconds.As many as 14 people were killed and 28 injured in the tragedy that occurred around 1.30 am outside the Sheetla Mata temple near a slope on Chinor Road. The truck crashed into several devotees and roadside shops before hitting the temple's entrance gate and bringing down a wall.14 killed, 28 injured as truck hits devotees near temple in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior Located about 20 km from the district headquarters, the 125-year-old shrine attracts lakhs of devotees during Navratri, many of whom walk barefoot to offer prayers.The scale of the devastation has left eyewitnesses questioning how a heavy commercial vehicle managed to reach the crowded shrine, given that vehicle movement is strictly restricted during the festival, with a designated parking facility set up nearly a kilometre away to prevent congestion.Saurabh, a devotee present near the spot, recalled the horror as the vehicle careened down the slope before anyone could react."The road near the temple was on a slope, and the truck came speeding down it. Nobody could understand what had happened. We realised the severity only when we heard people screaming," he said.While Saurabh managed to move ahead, his brother was trapped.Several others caught under the truck frantically struggled to pull themselves out, and some managed to do so, he said.The ordeal dragged on as efforts were made to move the paddy-laden truck.Five cranes were eventually deployed around 4 am to lift the overturned vehicle, Saurabh said, adding that police also arrived around the same time to assist in shifting the dead and injured to nearby hospitals.For some families, however, the nightmare did not end with the rescue operation.Kiran, who lost her 19-year-old son, alleged that the boy was still breathing after the accident, but police delayed shifting him to a private hospital, and the delay in transporting him to a government hospital ultimately cost him his life.Gajendra Prajapati, who runs a shop selling puja paraphernalia near the shrine, said the impact was so sudden and violent that the immediate surroundings were engulfed in thick smoke and dust.Angered by the accident, eyewitnesses demanded a thorough probe into how the truck reached the temple area despite restrictions on vehicular movement, calling for strict action against those responsible for the safety failure.Explaining the sequence of events, Gwalior Collector Ruchika Chouhan said the truck had crashed through police barricades and barreled towards the temple grounds at high speed.Two police personnel were also injured while attempting to stop the vehicle, she said, adding that the Regional Transport Office (RTO) has been directed to examine the truck.The Madhya Pradesh government has announced an ex-gratia assistance of Rs 4 lakh each to the kin of the deceased, Rs 2 lakh for those seriously injured, and Rs 50,000 for persons sustaining minor injuries, officials said.

Eyewitnesses described the Punjab-registered vehicle coming in "like a storm" through the no-entry zone near the shrine, triggering chaos within seconds.

primary_source.headline: Five killed after car, trying to escape pothole, crashes into state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed
primary_source.content: Beed: Five people, among them an 11-year-old boy, were killed after their car swerved to avoid potholes and collided with a state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed district on Sunday morning, police said.The accident occurred around 11 am at Shindewadi Cross Road on the Khamgaon-Pandharpur National Highway in Majalgaon tehsil, around 55 km from the district headquarters, an official said.He said that the victims, all residents of Majalgaon, were travelling towards Tuljapur in neighbouring Dharashiv district when their car crashed into a Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) bus coming from the opposite direction.The collision reduced the car to a mangled heap of metal, killing all five occupants on the spot, the official said.According to the police, the deceased have been identified as Omkar Mahadev Giri (24), Gajanan Mahadev Namdas (38), his son Samarth (11), Somnath Bade (23), and Anil Acharya (40).Speeding car crash triggers communal, moral and political row in KeralamCCTV footage from the area showed the speeding car lose control while attempting to avoid potholes on a bridge, leading to the head-on crash with the bus, the official said.The fatal crash triggered public anger over the deteriorating condition of roads on the Majalgaon-Telgaon stretch. Locals staged a road blockade alleging that substandard construction and poor maintenance had left fissures and uneven surfaces across the highway, turning the arterial road into an accident zone.Traffic came to a standstill for several hours on the highway due to the protest before senior police and district officials arrived at the scene, pacified the protesters, and restored traffic flow.

primary_source.headline: Opposition's 'low-level acts' reinforce need for PM Modi's leadership: Kangana Ranaut
primary_source.content: Raipur: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Sunday slammed opposition parties over their calls for regime change, stating that their "low-level acts" constantly remind the nation of the need for strong leadership under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Speaking to reporters at the Swami Vivekananda Airport here, the actor-politician cited recent unrest in France and global conflicts to emphasise that such developments make PM Modi's decisive leadership even more vital for India.Asked about the Opposition's remarks about regime change, she claimed, "Such low-level acts are repeatedly reminding the country that strong leadership is necessary. You saw what happened in France last night. Everything was set on fire, historical structures were destroyed, and looting took place."Delhi HC orders takedown of AI-generated obscene content on BJP MP Kangana RanautThe opposition parties have come under fire over senior advocate Prashant Bhushan’s "regime change" remark amid protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls.During a press conference earlier this week, Bhushan said spreading "disaffection" against a government is not a crime in a democracy, and that the struggle is now "really for a regime change". Several BJP leaders have reacted sharply to the remark.Ranaut said, "Everyone is watching the situation that has emerged around a possible Third World War. The Opposition is showing every day why India needs strong leadership in the form of Prime Minister Narendra Modi even more."The Mandi MP also condoled the death of 19 people in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata, calling the incident extremely tragic while urging citizens to avoid visiting overcrowded venues during festivals.At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening after a surge in the crowd amid rains.

primary_source.headline: Ebola outbreak spreads to eighth province in DR Congo, death toll tops 4,500
primary_source.content: The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, Congo's public health institute said on Sunday, confirming earlier Reuters reporting.The emergence of cases in the province, which borders Central African Republic, poses a new challenge for health authorities struggling to contain the outbreak.The National Institute for Biomedical Research confirmed two cases - including one death - in North Ubangi.Reuters reported on Thursday that two cases were confirmed in the province, citing two health officials. At the time, there was no official statement by Congolese authorities.WHO says Congo Ebola outbreak can still be brought under control within three monthsNorth Ubangi becomes the eighth province affected by the outbreak, alongside North Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, Sud-Kivu, Bas-Uele and South Ubangi.The outbreak, the worst Ebola epidemic in Congo's history, has already spread beyond the country's borders, with cases recorded in Uganda and seven infections confirmed in Kenya this month.Congo's latest situation report showed 67 new confirmed cases and 26 new deaths in the 24 hours to Oct.16, bringing the cumulative total to 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths since the outbreak began.The outbreak remains concentrated in eastern Congo, with Ituri province reporting 44 of the 67 new cases.

primary_source.headline: Kolkata stampede: Families mourn loss of loved ones as evening of festivity turned into heartache
primary_source.content: Kolkata: In a cruel twist of fate, pandal-hopping at the Chorbagan Durga Puja in Kolkata on a festive Saptami evening gave way to grief for a lifetime for many, who lost their loved ones in a tragic stampede that killed 19 people.Twenty-five others were injured in the stampede at the pandal in north Kolkata, following a crowd surge amid rain on Saturday evening. Of the dead, 13 were women and two minors.A rickshaw-puller, crying inconsolably, said he was at work on the fateful evening when he got the news of his daughter being fatally injured, and rushed to the Kolkata Medical College and Hospital with his wife."Durga Puja will never come in our lives again; we have lost our Durga," said the distraught father of 17-year-old Barnali Halder."Every year during Durga Puja, my daughter will come alive in my heart," he said.Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampedeBarnali, a student of Class-11, had gone pandal-hopping with six of her friends, he said."My daughter and another girl could not make it, while the others in the group managed to escape," he said.The resident of Gauranganagar in New Town said those in charge of crowd management should have been more active when the number of visitors swelled, maintaining that it was difficult for people to find their way out of the dimly-lit pandal during the rush.Saurav Mondal, who stays in Kumartuli, lost his mother Mithu Mondal in the tragedy."In the melee, my mother and I fell down. At one point, I felt I would not be able to come out alive as several people had fallen atop us," he said.Saurav said a police officer managed to pull him out."My mother died on the spot," he said, lamenting that there were “very few” police personnel and volunteers inside the pandal.A woman from Bihar’s Muzaffarpur lost her husband in the stampede, family members said."They arrived in Kolkata on Saturday morning to be a part of the Durga Puja festivities in the city for the first time, but little did they know that this would turn out to be their last," said a family member, at whose home the couple had lunch before visiting the Chorbagan pandal.The Chorbagan Durga Puja, popular among revellers for its theme-based pandals, is situated off the arterial Chittaranjan Avenue in north Kolkata and lies in the vicinity of several other well-known community pujas.

stories.primary_headline: Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govt

primary_source.headline: Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govt
primary_source.content:
Kolkata: The Mamata All India Trinamool Congress launched a sharp attack on West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and Kolkata Police over a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal that claimed 19 lives, bringing the name of the CM's nephew Debdeep Adhikari, listed as chief patron of the Chorbagan Sarbojonin Durgotsab Samity, under the spotlight.The opposition party questioned the preparedness of the authorities and alleged that inadequate crowd management, a lack of police presence and the absence of adequate emergency arrangements contributed to the tragedy at the popular Chorbagan pandal on Saturday evening.In a series of posts on social media, the Mamata AITC alleged there were no adequate police personnel, civic volunteers or ambulances at the venue when the situation spiralled out of control.It cited accounts of locals and eyewitnesses to question the security arrangements and the administration's response.Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede"Where was the security and emergency response when people needed you most?" the party asked on its social media handles, targeting the Kolkata Police over the alleged lapses.The party's national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee also questioned the alleged involvement of the chief minister's nephew in the puja organising committee and demanded accountability from the ruling establishment.Referring to the committee's list of office-bearers, he asked, "When will you put the culprit nephew in jail, Suvendu Babu?"Will @KolkataPolice take any action against the first three names or are they being protected by the illegitimate CM himself?Debdeep Adhikari - Chief PatronNEPHEW OF @SuvenduWBVijay Ojha - Chairman@BJP4Bengal MLATamoghna Ghosh - Chief AdvisorBJP District President, North… https://t.co/5PMqi75arE pic.twitter.com/a7M5mjb9VQ&mdash; All India Trinamool Congress (@AITCofficial) October 18, 2026
 

In support of its claim, the party shared purported publicity material of the organising committee of the Chorbagan puja which listed Debdeep Adhikari as its chief patron, Vijay Ojha, the BJP MLA of the local Jorasanko constituency as the committee chairman and BJP's North Kolkata district president Tamaghna Ghosh as its chief advisor.It demanded that those connected with the event be held accountable.Mamata AITC spokesperson and MLA Kunal Ghosh further alleged that the previous puja committee was "forced" to step down following the change of guard in power, and was "captured" by a new committee.Ghosh posted on Facebook a letter, purportedly written by former puja secretary Jayanta Banerjee on July 17, tendering his resignation and relieving other committee members from their responsibilities."The previous committee in Chorbagan was allegedly forced to resign, following which a new set of people 'captured' the new committee. Take a look at the resignation letters of the former committee members and the list of members of the new committee," Ghosh wrote, bringing the puja committee's current leadership under scrutiny.Acting on a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder registered at the local Girish Park police station, law enforcers on Sunday arrested seven people, including the puja committee general secretary Raj Kumar Sewda and vice president Santanu Dubey.Responding to a question on the alleged involvement of Debdeep Adhikari in the affairs of the Chorbagan Puja, BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said he had no knowledge about the matter.Kolkata pandal stampede: Seven, including Chorbagan Durga Puja organisers, arrested"To the best of my knowledge, the chief minister's nephew is a minor and stays in Kanthi in Purba Medinipur district. How can he get involved in a Kolkata puja? I do not wish to indulge in politics over this tragedy. I am quite devastated at the scale of this horrible incident," Bhattacharya told reporters on Saturday evening after visiting the spot where the stampede took place.Adhikari, in a message on early Sunday morning, strongly condemned the attempts to politicise the tragedy and lashed out at critics, stating the entire top brass of the state police and administration was doing everything in its power to offer relief to the victims and their families."Without blaming anyone, I would say that last year there were two incidents, the first where 13 people died of electrocution in waterlogged areas and second, where over a hundred people were washed away in flash floods in the upper reaches of West Bengal. You had seen the role of the then chief minister at the time," Adhikari said."I am not comparing them with the current tragedy, only saying this because things are being written on social media. I will ask them to refrain from making such comments. People will spit on you; if you keep doing it," he added.The stampede unfolded around 7.30-7.40 pm on Saturday, as a large crowd gathered at the pandal amid rainfall. The crush occurred near an exit and a narrow approach lane, with the sudden rush and people falling over one another triggering chaos. The exact sequence of events and the possible role of crowd-control failures are being investigated.Adhikari, meanwhile, has announced a probe into the incident. Police detained organisers, private security personnel and others involved in managing the crowd for questioning, while investigators are examining possible lapses in security and the management of entry and exit routes.The chief minister has also said he would request the Calcutta High Court chief justice to facilitate an inquiry led by a judge.The state government has announced compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a government job for a member of each deceased person's family, besides Rs 5 lakh for each injured person and coverage of their medical expenses.The tragedy has cast a shadow over Durga Puja celebrations in the city, with the authorities moving to inspect other crowded pandals and review safety arrangements to prevent a recurrence.

stories.primary_headline: Bus attack puts spotlight on safety of Kashmiri travellers, truckers

primary_source.headline: Bus attack puts spotlight on safety of Kashmiri travellers, truckers
primary_source.content:
Srinagar: An attack on a Jammu and Kashmir-bound luxury sleeper bus carrying around 40 passengers near Kurukshetra in Haryana has renewed concerns over the safety of Kashmiri travellers outside the Union Territory, with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah seeking stringent action against those responsible.The bus, travelling from Delhi to Srinagar, was allegedly targeted with stones and bricks by unidentified persons, leaving an elderly Kashmiri passenger injured and others traumatised, according to officials and social media accounts.The Chief Minister’s Office said it had taken up the incident with the Haryana government, which assured prompt and stringent action in accordance with the law.“This unfortunate incident should never have taken place,” Abdullah said on X, urging the government led by Nayab Singh Saini and Haryana Police to catch the culprits and ensure such incidents were not repeated.This unfortunate incident should never have taken place. I hope the Haryana government lead by @NayabSainiBJP ji & @police_haryana catch the culprits & take action to ensure these things don’t happen again. https://t.co/7syQ37P2oP&mdash; Omar Abdullah (@OmarAbdullah) October 18, 2026
 

Separately, Kashmir’s chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq expressed concern over the attack, saying reports of threats against Jammu and Kashmir-registered vehicles were causing anxiety among people. He called for the safety of Kashmiri travellers to be ensured and strict legal action against those responsible.Jammu and Kashmir National Conference leader Imran Nabi Dar had earlier highlighted the alleged attack on X, describing it as a hate crime.A video circulating on social media purportedly shows damage to the bus operated by Star World Ventures, including shattered windows and broken tail lights. The motive behind the incident has not been independently established.'You are bloody sh*t': IAS officer’s clash with woman colleague snowballs into major row in Jammu and KashmirThe episode has brought into focus concerns over the safety of Kashmiris travelling for work, education and trade. Truck drivers transporting the Valley’s apple harvest to markets across India are particularly dependent on safe and uninterrupted highway movement.Kashmiri truckers have faced similar incidents in the past. In November 2022, a driver from Kulgam was allegedly assaulted by toll plaza employees in Punjab, prompting police to register an FIR. In 2015, Zahid Ahmed, a Kashmiri trucker, died after a petrol-bomb attack in Udhampur amid rumours of cow slaughter.Mutton transporters have also alleged harassment and unauthorised fee collection at checkpoints in Punjab. The dispute escalated in June 2026 when a strike by traders disrupted supplies in Kashmir. Abdullah subsequently wrote to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, seeking intervention to ensure the safe movement of livestock vehicles.

primary_source.headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending
primary_source.content: In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable.It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Actor Imran Khan not Indian citizen, shouldn't have been at Mumbai protests: Union Min Chirag Paswan

primary_source.headline: Actor Imran Khan not Indian citizen, shouldn't have been at Mumbai protests: Union Min Chirag Paswan
primary_source.content: Patna: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Sunday said Bollywood actor Imran Khan was "not an Indian citizen"; and he should have stayed away from protests against SIR, which the MP called "attempts to create anarchy, backed by foreign powers".Speaking to reporters here, Paswan also criticised Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for going ahead with political engagements in Goa unlike Union Home Minister Amit Shah who showed "sensitivity" by cancelling all his scheduled programmes in Kolkata, where 19 people were killed in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal.The Hajipur MP, who, incidentally, tried his hand in films before entering politics, was responding to queries about the "leave India" notice issued to Khan, an OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card holder, who has been charged with violating the Foreigners' Act.'Leave India': Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against 'illegal, bad in law' notice by Mumbai police, FRRO issues him show-cause notice"I like the actor and his work. But he should have realised that he did not become an Indian citizen just by virtue of having worked in the country for so long. If citizens take part in protests here, I respect that. But when foreign nationals do that it is a matter of concern. As part of the Union government, I am concerned over the attempts to create anarchy in the country, with the backing of foreign powers," Paswan said.Notably, Khan is a nephew of superstar Amir Khan. He was born in the US and holds American citizenship, though he was brought up in India and has been active in the film industry for over a decade.The actor received the notice days after turning up at a demonstration staged in Mumbai to press for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.Paswan, who heads Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), also expressed grief over the loss of lives in Kolkata, and lauded Shah for showing "sensitivity" by cancelling his programmes in the city.Referring to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's scheduled rally in Goa, where assembly polls are due in a few months, the Union minister said, "It shows the difference in priorities. On the one hand, we have our home minister who is sensitive towards a tragedy, and on the other, we have the opposition for which nothing matters more than politics."

In a 2017 letter he signed along with 20 other US senators, Rubio called for “strong multilateral sanctions against specific senior Burmese military officials associated with the gross human rights abuses”. Those responsible for the atrocities should be prosecuted, he argued.In the years since, the Myanmar military’s crimes have only increased. What was then deemed ethnic cleansing of the Rohingya is now widely viewed, including by the US, as genocide. What little democracy existed in Myanmar was eradicated in 2021 when Aung San Suu Kyi was arrested and imprisoned and her party’s election victory overturned, and the military took full control. stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara to feature special tableaux on Army, Navy, Air Force and more

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara to feature special tableaux on Army, Navy, Air Force and more
primary_source.content: Mysuru: With the countdown to the Dasara Jamboo Savari procession underway, more than 1,000 artists are busy preparing 53 tableaux at Bandipalya and the Karnataka Exhibition Authority grounds in Mysuru on Saturday.Seven special tableaux will showcase Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Tibetan settlements, Tulu Nadu, the Koragajja community and other themes. Another 18 tableaux by state government departments will depict initiatives and institutions, including the Bharat Jodo Yuva Sangha and the Tourism Department. Eleven tableaux representing the Central government will feature the Indian Army, Navy, Air Force and others. There will also be tableaux highlighting the specialities of 16 districts.Besides these, the procession will feature Ambari buses carrying sandalwood stars and sports personalities, an Air Force bus, Army and Navy bands, and Hallikar oxen.Activists demand volume caps on Mysuru Palace concerts to protect Dasara elephantsArtist S C Suresh was seen giving the finishing touches to tableaux showcasing the specialities of Hassan district along with his 10-member team. The tableaux will feature Booker Prize winner Banu Mushtaq, the Yettinahole Integrated Drinking Water Supply Project, a memorial for Dasara veteran Arjuna in the Yesalur range, Someshwara Temple and folk art forms such as Chikkimela and Togalu Gombeyaata.Artist Krishna Tiptur, who has won prizes five times, is working with his 22-member team on the tableaux representing Tumakuru district. The displays will feature nuclear scientist Raja Ramanna, who hailed from Tumakuru district, Devarayanadurga and the proposed Metro project. They will also highlight Tumakuru's status as an industrial, coconut and sports hub, including its international cricket and hockey stadiums.KSRTC Mysuru Rural Divisional Controller H T Veeresh was supervising work on the KSRTC tableaux, which will showcase buses ranging from the 'Banashankari' model of the 1970s to the latest models.Artist N Rajesh and his team were giving the finishing touches to tableaux representing Tulu Nadu, featuring Kambala, Kukke Subramanya Temple and other attractions.

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara airshow: Surya Kiran's dazzling display cut short by rain

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara airshow: Surya Kiran's dazzling display cut short by rain
primary_source.content: Mysuru: The Suryakiran Aerobatic Team (SKAT) of the Indian Air Force, enthralled the jam-packed crowd at Bannimantap ground with their spectacular aerial display during Dasara Airshow in Mysuru on Sunday morning. However, due to rain and inclement weather conditions, the air warriors could only perform three horizontal manoeuvres, including the arrow manoeuvre with nine Hawk Mk 132 aircraft, in the blue sky canvas of Mysuru. The display was complemented by saffron, white and green smoke trails. The team, known for its precision, coordination, synchronisation, discipline and teamwork, performed with all the aircraft operating as a cohesive unit.Mysuru Dasara to feature special tableaux on Army, Navy, Air Force and moreMysuru: Farmers' Dasara turns into platform to inspire community towards independent livelihood, women empowermentThe people who had gathered after the gates of the ground opened at 9 am could witness the show for about 10 minutes from 11.20 am. They were disappointed as the team could not continue the show in view of the safety of pilots and the aircraft due to weather conditions. However, people returned with hope, as the show will be held on Monday too. On Monday, the Surya Kiran team will be flying all the nine aircraft, manufactured under licence by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL). They plan to showcase a series of intricate aerobatic manoeuvres, including both horizontal and vertical ones. Signature manoeuvres such as loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and the DNA manoeuvres can also be witnessed.Set up in 1996, the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team has a legacy of representing the Indian Air Force and the nation at air shows and public events across India and abroad. With over 800 displays to its credit, the team is inspiring generations of aviation enthusiasts and young Indians to consider a career in the Indian Air Force.  The display forms part of the team’s continued endeavour to bring the Indian Air Force closer to the people of the country. The show has been an opportunity for people to witness the synergy between man and machine, where every manoeuvre reflects the dedication, skill and teamwork that define the Indian Air Force.

stories.primary_headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage

primary_source.headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: Keralam Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan on Sunday expressed dissatisfaction with the Devaswom Board's preparations for the upcoming annual Sabarimala pilgrimage season.The minister's remarks came a day after he and Chief Minister V D Satheesan visited the various places associated with the Sabarimala pilgrimage to review preparations and facilities for the upcoming season.After the review meeting, the CM said that all arrangements related to temple rituals and prasadam were under the control of the Devaswom Board, and its president has assured that there will be no shortage of prasadam or other facilities at the shrine.On Sunday, Muraleedharan told a TV channel that repair and renovation of the plant manufacturing the 'aravana payasam' prasadam has not been completed yet.He also said that there was an apparent lack of coordination between the Board and the police with regard to crowd control.BJP steps up attack on Keralam govt over Sabarimala arrangementsThe minister said that his two main concerns were regulating the large number of devotees who arrived for the pilgrimage and ensuring a sufficient supply of 'appam' and 'aravana' for the pilgrims.'Aravana' -- a thick, sweet dessert made from red rice, jaggery, ghee, cardamom powder, and ginger powder -- and 'appam' -- a traditional sweet rice cake/fritter made with ingredients like rice and jaggery -- are the two primary 'prasadam' at the Lord Ayyappa shrine at Sabarimala."I am not completely satisfied with the steps being taken to ensure the prasadam sufficiency. The contract for the rice has not yet been finalised by the Board. I have been told that the repair and renovation of the plant will be completed by November 5 and production will be started," Muraleedharan said.He said that he has told the Board to give specific attention to these issues.The minister said that 29,000 devotees reached the shrine on Saturday ahead of the commencement of the 'Thula masam' puja on Sunday and currently there were two lakh aravana in stock."I have told the Board to take extra care regarding the matter up to October 22 (when the shrine will close again). After that, they have to ensure things are much better," he said.The Sabarimala shrine will be open for five days during the 'Thula masam' -- the third month in the traditional Malayalam calendar -- from October 18 to October 22.Muraleedharan also said that there was a delay in the completion of temple maintenance works."The government is doing all that has to be done," he added.The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple will open on November 17 for the 41-day Mandalam pilgrimage season.

sources.headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage

brief_bullets: Thiruvananthapuram: Keralam Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan on Sunday expressed dissatisfaction with the Devaswom Board's preparations for the upcoming annual Sabarimala pilgrimage season.

stories.primary_headline: 'BJP is not India': Pooja Bedi voices support for anti-CEC protest, slams police crackdown

primary_source.headline: 'BJP is not India': Pooja Bedi voices support for anti-CEC protest, slams police crackdown
primary_source.content:
Actor Pooja Bedi has voiced her support for the ongoing anti-CEC protest demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and criticised the ruling party Bhartiya Janta Party (BJP) for detaining demonstrators.In a video posted on her Instagram, alongside a detailed caption, Bedi asked the citizens to "speak", urging that its "time to make a difference".Bedi began the video by stressing that criticising the BJP is not anti-national."Speaking up against the BJP is not anti-national because the BJP is not India and India is not the BJP. India existed before the BJP and India will exist after the BJP. What we need to question is a government we have reportedly elected to uphold our democracy. Where are our rights today? Who is the anti-national?," she said in the video.She continued, "If the BJP is arresting our protesters, the young kids on the streets from holding peaceful demonstrations, which is a democratic right that we all have, who is anti-national?"        View this post on Instagram            
 Calling the government tyrannical for oppressing voices, she added, "Are the people voicing their opinions, frustrations and demanding accountability from the government anti-nationals? Or is it the government who is turning around and suppressing their voices in the most tyrannical, oppressive way, is that the democracy we voted for? Is that the kind of country leadership we are looking at?"Bedi also questioned how protestors are getting "five-day judicial custody for trespassing, while rapists and murderers get bail in a day."She went on to question the citizens for staying silent amid all the unrest and asked if it's a dictatorship that we have voted for, adding, "What is the India that you want to be proud of and take into the new era with our wonderful children being a part of this incredible India we keep talking about?"She concluded the video by urging citizens to "speak up" and "educate the people around you about what is happening" in the country."This cannot continue. We cannot just sit by mutely and watch our children trying to protect our country that we have let down. We have let down the country and we have let down our children. Please speak up and be a national," she concluded.'Dissent not anti-national': Huma Qureshi, Sonakshi, Anurag Kashyap & others voice support for EC-SIR stirIn the caption posted alongside the video, she urged people to become the "torch bearer for your democracy"."In an opressive regime that seeks to control your voice, your media, your feed, ... its time to be the torch bearer for your democracy.create awareness..... shine a torch on their brutality, lawlessness, high handedness and undemocratic actions (sic)," she wrote, adding, "Awareness leads to impact and change. You are NEEDED. Your country needs you. The children of india need you. The democratic future of india depends on YOU! (sic)."Meanwhile, several other celebrities including actor Imran Khan, Kiran Rao, Sonakshi Sinha, Huma Qureshi, Vijay Varma, Naseeruddin Shah and Anurag Kashyap have voiced support for the protest.

stories.primary_headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings

primary_source.headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
primary_source.content: Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to  “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.” One employee reportedly described an “eternal pressure at Anthropic to move as fast as possible and use Claude for everything.” In an April 2026 survey, 27% of employees said they had become more productive because of Claude  and 20% said their job had shifted “from actually doing work to managing Claudes”; apparently one engineered compared this to babysitting: “When you are babysitting, every child brings to you concerns with an equal demand for your attention and the various [Claudes] also do that.” In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized. Unsurprisingly, the report argues that AI adoption has made the company more productive, as indicated by “more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.” The company acknowledges that “more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact,” but it also hasn’t found any indications that code quality is declining.

stories.primary_headline: Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team to stage aerial show in Mysuru on Oct 18 and 19

primary_source.headline: Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team to stage aerial show in Mysuru on Oct 18 and 19
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: The Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team (SKAT) of the Indian Air Force, renowned for its precision, discipline and teamwork, is set to enthral the people of Mysuru with a spectacular aerial display on October 18 and 19 during the Dasara.&nbsp;Flying nine Hawk Mk 132 aircraft, manufactured under licence by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), the team will showcase a series of intricate aerobatic manoeuvres that promise to leave spectators spellbound. Signature manoeuvres such as loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and the iconic DNA manoeuvre will demonstrate exceptional precision, coordination and synchronisation. Performed in close formation, with nine aircraft operating as one cohesive unit, the display will be complemented by vibrant saffron, white and green smoke trails, adding to the spectacle in the skies over Mysuru.Established in 1996, the SKAT has a proud legacy of representing the Indian Air Force and the nation at air shows and public events across India and abroad. With over 850 displays to its credit, the team has become a symbol of the Service’s flying excellence, discipline and professionalism, inspiring generations of aviation enthusiasts and young Indians. Every display is the culmination of extensive training, meticulous planning and complete trust among the pilots and the support team.Mysuru, celebrated for its magnificent palaces, architectural splendour and rich cultural heritage, provides a distinguished setting for this aerial showcase. The display will offer the people of the city an opportunity to witness the remarkable synergy between man and machine, where every manoeuvre reflects the dedication, skill and teamwork that define the Indian Air Force.The display forms part of the SKAT’s continued endeavour to bring the Indian Air Force closer to the people of the country. Through its spectacular aerial performances, the team provides the public with an opportunity to witness the skill, precision and professionalism of the Service, while inspiring young Indians to aspire to excellence and consider a career in the Indian Air Force.The SKAT looks forward to enthralling the people of Mysuru with its signature aerial manoeuvres and bringing a memorable display of precision and aerial excellence to the city.Squadron Leader Vikram of the SKAT spoke to DH on the sidelines of the press conference in Bengaluru on Saturday:&nbsp;Excerpts:Q) What special manoeuvres have you planned for the display? Are they new?A) One of the special highlights of our Mysuru display will be a series of flybys by all nine aircraft in formations similar to the various monuments around this historic city. We invite everyone to look out for this special formation during the display. Along with this special tribute, we will bring the thrill and excitement of our signature aerobatic manoeuvres to the skies of Mysuru, including loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and our iconic DNA manoeuvre. Through these manoeuvres, performed with precision and synchronisation by all nine aircraft, we hope to thrill the people of Mysuru and give them an unforgettable experience.Q) Have you customised this particular show for Karnataka and the special occasion?A) We are delighted to be back in Mysuru and to perform before the people of Karnataka. We will be presenting a special display that connects with the local heritage and cultural identity of this region. Through this performance, we hope to celebrate the rich cultural heritage of Mysuru and Karnataka, connect meaningfully with the people of this beautiful city, and inspire the youth of our country to aspire to join the Indian Air Force and serve the nation.&nbsp;The display is also dedicated to the spirit of the Indian Air Force as it celebrates 94 years of service to the nation, reflecting our shared pride and commitment to the country.

stories.primary_headline: Ember’s new temperature-controlled mug makes my nightly tea ritual even better

primary_source.headline: Ember’s new temperature-controlled mug makes my nightly tea ritual even better
primary_source.content: Ember first introduced its smart mug in 2016 to solve a problem most coffee and tea drinkers know all too well: getting distracted for a few minutes, only to return to a lukewarm drink. Now, the company is back with its third-generation mug, which brings a handful of practical upgrades. The biggest change is that you no longer have to open the app to adjust your drink’s temperature. Instead, you can use the button on the bottom of the mug to cycle through five preset temperatures, starting at 125 degrees Fahrenheit. Each press raises the temperature by five degrees, up to a maximum of 145 degrees, so you can easily make your drink a little hotter with each click. Honestly, this is the feature I ended up using the most during my time testing out the mug. At night, when I’m curled up in bed with a book and a cup of tea, my phone is usually somewhere across the room. Being able to adjust my drink without getting up to find it is a small convenience, but one I genuinely appreciate. That said, I do have one complaint: the button is located on the bottom of the mug. It’s a peculiar design choice when you’re dealing with a cup full of hot liquid, and it isn’t particularly easy to press, either. I often found myself tilting the mug and pressing down firmly to get it to respond. So, while I appreciate the addition of on-mug controls, I wish Ember had made the button easier to reach. If you prefer using your phone, the Ember app still offers plenty of customization. After pairing the mug with your phone over Bluetooth, you can choose presets based on what you’re drinking. Ember recommends 136 degrees Fahrenheit for black coffee, 132 degrees for green tea, and 142 degrees for lemon water. You can also create your own temperature presets, which is handy if you like your drinks a little hotter or cooler than the recommended settings. The Mug 3 also comes with a few other upgrades, including a sliding lid designed to help prevent spills. The mug can also keep your drink at its desired temperature for up to three hours on a single charge. And it’s the first mug in Ember’s lineup to be top-rack dishwasher-safe, making cleanup easier. (Just keep in mind that it isn’t microwave-safe.)

stories.primary_headline: Move over, pervert glasses – the latest toxic trend is robogroping

primary_source.headline: Move over, pervert glasses – the latest toxic trend is robogroping
primary_source.content: Whenever a new technology is created, it will, without exception, immediately be used to harass girls and womenYou may be familiar with rule 34 of the internet, which states that if something exists or can be imagined, there will almost certainly be online porn of it. Now let me introduce my rule 35: whenever a new technology is created, it will, without exception, immediately be used to harass girls and women.See, for example, Meta’s “pervert glasses”. As anyone could have foreseen, putting a tiny camera and microphone into smartglasses would immediately lead to people using them to record and harass women. Lo and behold, that is exactly what happened. So-called manfluencers have filmed themselves trying to flirt with women in public spaces and then uploaded the footage to TikTok. The women in these videos are often not aware they’ve been recorded until their identities are shared online and they are harassed by strangers. And what’s Meta doing about this? It’s instituted a few bans and made some privacy updates, but doesn’t seem to have an appetite to properly solve the problem. Indeed, at the Meta Connect 2026 keynote, Mark Zuckerberg did not feel the need to apologize to the women whose lives have been upended by his technology. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers

primary_source.headline: Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers
primary_source.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday participated in the party's 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Margao, walking two kilometres alongside party workers and leaders.Gandhi arrived at Dabolim airport in the afternoon to join the mass outreach programme. He is scheduled to address a public gathering at the Margao Cricket Club (MCC) ground later in the day.Among those who accompanied him during the yatra were AICC Goa desk in-charge Manikrao Thakare, co-in-charge Dr Anjali Nimbalkar, Leader of Opposition Yuri Alemao and Goa Pradesh Congress Committee president Girish Chodankar.The 27-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', led by Alemao and Chodankar, began on September 22 and concluded on Sunday. The campaign covered all 40 Assembly constituencies in Goa as the Congress seeks to strengthen its grassroots network ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Rahul Gandhi to address Goa rally as Congress wraps up 28-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra'The party described the 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', which translates to a campaign to protect Goa, as a movement to safeguard the state's land, environment, cultural heritage and identity.Throughout the campaign, the Congress highlighted concerns over land conversion, alleged land grabbing, unemployment, corruption and public safety, while emphasising the need to preserve Goa's distinct social and cultural identity.The yatra also aimed to engage with local communities and bring development-related issues to the forefront of political discussions.With the 2027 Goa Assembly elections approaching, the Congress is seeking to expand its grassroots presence and mobilise support across constituencies, including those currently represented by the ruling BJP.

sources.headline: Pope Leo to gradually resume papal activities since removal of cancerous tumour

brief_bullets: Pontiff thanks people for their prayers as he recovers from operation on his lung.

Pope Leo told a crowd gathered in St Peter’s Square on Sunday that he would “gradually resume” his activities, at his first appearance before the faithful since undergoing an operation to remove a cancerous tumour from his lung.
The Catholic leader, 71, was greeted with applause as he appeared unaided at the window of the Vatican’s Apostolic Palace to deliver his Sunday angelus.
It was his first public appearance since making the shock announcement at the previous Sunday’s address that a small nodule had been found on his lung.

It was his first public appearance since making the shock announcement at the previous Sunday’s address that a small nodule had been found on his lung. stories.primary_headline: 'Mujhe kidnap hi kar liya tha': Reality TV star Akanksha Choudhary narrates 'deeply disturbing' incident; accuses event organisers of misconduct

primary_source.headline: 'Mujhe kidnap hi kar liya tha': Reality TV star Akanksha Choudhary narrates 'deeply disturbing' incident; accuses event organisers of misconduct
primary_source.content: Reality TV star Akanksha Choudhary, who was recently seen in Lock Upp 2, has narrated her ordeal, making serious allegations against the Navratri event organisers in Pune.Taking to her Instagram Stories, Choudhary accused the organisers of mismanagement, non-payment of her dues, and "kidnapping" her.The event, which was held at Pedkar Grounds in Pune, was organised by three members of the management team, who, according to Choudhary, were 18 years old.&nbsp;In a series of Instagram Stories, Choudhary narrated her ordeal of how she made to wait till 10.30 since no one from the management team came to pick her up for the event and that she had to reach the event venue by herself.She then accused the organisers of scamming her, along with other artists, and not clearing their dues.Choudhary further added that the situation became even more uncomfortable when she was made to sit in a car and taken inside the venue ground.Screengrab of Akanksha Choudhary's Instagram Story.She claimed that the car was stopped right in front of the audience despite her telling the organisers that she cannot enter the venue without her team as she does not feel safe.She further alleged all her pleas went unheard and the young organisers kept laughing at her."Zabardasti gaadi mein bitakar, ground mein chhod diya, and in front of the audience they stopped. Main chilla rahi hoon ki main andar nahi ja sakti, meri team nahi hai mere saath. It is not safe, aur yeh bacche hass rahe hain, meri baat nahi sun rahe hain. Itna stupid management. Chor hain yeh ekdum, sabka payment le liya, use kar liya," Choudhary said.Screengrab of Akanksha Choudhary's Instagram Story.She further went on to call the incident a kidnapping-like situation, and added, "Mujhe kidnap hi kar liya tha sort of, jab maine thappad maari unko, tab rukhe woh. Unpe case sab karungi, chhodungi nahi main."In the following Instagram Stories, Choudhary also claimed that she, along with her team members, were subjected to intimation, threats and mental harassment, from the organisers who claimed that they belong to influential families and that they will handle the matter in their "own way".Calling the incident "deeply disturbing", Choudhary threatened legal action against those involved.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy

primary_source.headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy
primary_source.content: Critics mock it as raunchy trash – but this enchanting genre is much older, and wilder, than you might imagineThere’s a popular genre, filled with beautiful, human-sized fairies having sex with humans (often quite violent sex, but the people reading it seem to enjoy it). Word is that it’s badly written and unashamedly escapist – all golden, glittering palaces, wild adventure and, of course, gorgeous fairies. It’s certainly popular – plenty of the stories have been translated into numerous languages, spreading across continents. Serious commentators are sure it spells bad news: at best, it’s just a load of trash; at worst, it’s actively leading people astray. Most damningly of all, women produce and consume it. Welcome to the 12th century, where fairy romance is all the rage. Sound familiar?The romantasy that fills our shelves and bestseller lists – from Sarah J Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses to Callie Hart’s Quicksilver – is not a new genre, but part of a centuries-old heritage. You only need to look at the medieval predecessors of the modern romantasy novel to understand why it’s enjoyed by millions and why, even after hundreds of years, fairy romance has such power over us – and why there are still those who want to diminish and dismiss it. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Vance admits 'imperfect' rhetoric over 'indentured servants' remark on H-1B workers

primary_source.headline: Vance admits 'imperfect' rhetoric over 'indentured servants' remark on H-1B workers
primary_source.content: Washington: US Vice President J D Vance has admitted that his rhetoric has been "imperfect” when he referred to foreign professionals holding H-1 B visas as “indentured servants”.He also clarified that he meant US companies and the visa system, not H-1B visa holders.India had objected strongly to the language used to describe foreign professionals calling the terminology "deeply offensive" and saying it carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations.Speaking at the CBS News Townhall event on Saturday, Vance insisted his criticism targeted the visa system that gives employers too much power over foreign employees, who can be sent back to their country of origin and effectively treated as “indentured servants”.“I would say, and to the extent that my rhetoric has been imperfect here, that's on me,” Vance said in response to a question from an Indian immigrant, who became a US citizen five years ago and voted for President Donald Trump.The Vice President said his comments were "not a criticism of the H-1B holder.""...Is when they come in on an H-1B, they're very often coming in, and the company is certifying that they're doing a job that they can't find an alternative American labour applicant for. And importantly, their visa is their only lifeline to the United States of America. So when I say an indentured servant, that's not a criticism of the H-1B visa holder. That's a criticism of a company that brings a person in," Vance said.J D Vance calls H-1B workers 'indentured servants', accuses Microsoft of visa abuse"It's a criticism of the visa system that allows people to be treated effectively as indentured servants that can be shipped back to their country of origin," Vance said.He also mentioned his South Indian in-laws while calling for a balance between welcoming foreign professionals and protecting American workers."You know where my family comes from, and I love my mother-in-law and father-in-law who immigrated from South India, and obviously their daughter, born in the United States of America, is now the second lady, and I’m very proud of her, and I love her very much."His wife, Usha Vance, is the daughter of Indian immigrants."I will tell you that nobody's perfect, certainly not me. But my goal here is not to dehumanise any immigrant, and in fact, I love a number of immigrants,” Vance said.Earlier this month, the US suspended several firms, including Indian IT companies, from a programme that lets foreign workers apply for green cards, arguing that the practice has shut Americans out of the job market. Vice President Vance made the announcement.Indian professionals account for over 70 per cent of all approved H-1B petitions annually.Vance referred to foreign workers hired on H1-B visas as “foreign indentured servants” and the companies using the programme as “visa mills”.

stories.primary_headline: Bengaluru continues to lead in India’s occupied office stock

primary_source.headline: Bengaluru continues to lead in India’s occupied office stock
primary_source.content: Mumbai: India’s occupied office stock across the country’s eight leading markets grew 7% year-on-year (YoY) to 917.7 million square feet (mn sq ft) as of September 30, 2026, up from 859.4 mn sq ft a year earlier, according to Knight Frank India. The 58.3 mn sq ft increase underscores sustained demand for office space across major commercial hubs, with Bengaluru retaining its position as the largest market and Pune crossing the 100 mn sq ft mark.Bengaluru retained its position as the country’s largest office market, with occupied stock rising 9% YoY to 227.9 mn sq ft. Pune’s occupied office stock reached 101.0 mn sq ft as of September 30, 2026, registering a 9% YoY increase from 92.4 mn sq ft as of September 30, 2025. Hyderabad recorded the strongest growth among markets, with occupied stock expanding by 11% to 119.8 mn sq ft.From startups to global giants: How coworking became big business in IndiaIn a press statement, Viral Desai, international partner and senior executive director, Occupier Strategy Solutions, Industrial & Logistics, Capital Markets & Retail, said, “India’s office markets continue to demonstrate resilience, supported by business expansion and the evolving workplace requirements of occupiers. Pune crossing 100 mn sq ft of occupied office stock is an important milestone for the market, reflecting its growing scale as a commercial real estate destination. At the same time, sustained growth across Bengaluru, Hyderabad and other leading markets highlights the breadth of office market activity across the country.”Key highlights Bengaluru: Retained its position as India’s largest office market, with occupied stock increasing 9% YoY from 208.3 mn sq ft to 227.9 mn sq ft as of September 30, 2026.NCR: Continued to rank as the country’s second-largest office market, with occupied stock rising 2% YoY to 178.3 mn sq ft from 175 mn sq ft.Mumbai: Recorded occupied office stock of 148.2 mn sq ft, marking a 5% YoY increase from 141.5 mn sq ft as of September 30, 2025.Hyderabad: Occupied stock grew 11% YoY to 119.8 million sq ft from 108.3 mn sq ft, representing the fastest growth among the four markets with over 100 mn sq ft of occupied stock.

stories.primary_headline: Flight services at Thiruvananthapuram airport to be suspended on Oct 20 for 5 hrs

primary_source.headline: Flight services at Thiruvananthapuram airport to be suspended on Oct 20 for 5 hrs
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: Flight services at the international airport here will be temporarily suspended for five hours on October 20 to enable the traditional "Arattu" procession of Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple to pass through the runway, TIAL said on Sunday.The ritual is in line with a decades-old practice involving the Travancore Royals.The Thiruvananthapuram International Airport Ltd (TIAL), in a statement, said the flight services would be suspended from 4 pm to 9 pm on October 20 to facilitate the 'Alpassi Arattu' procession by the Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple.It said the updated timings of the flights are available with the respective airlines.Bengaluru's KIA and Vancouver airport sign sister airport agreement to boost direct flights, cargo tradeThe airport has been pausing operations and rescheduling flights twice every year for decades to enable the bi-annual centuries-old ceremonial procession of the shrine to pass through the runway.The practice of the temple procession passing through the route to reach the Shangumugham beach for the holy bath of the idols began centuries ago, and it has been continuing even after the establishment of the airport in 1932.When the airport was constructed in the particular place, the then Travancore King Sree Chithira Thirunal had made it clear that the facility would be open to the public for 363 days in a year and for two days for Lord Padmanabha, the titular deity of the royal family, according to historians.The royal-era ritual has been continuing even after the Adani Group took over the management of the airport.

stories.primary_headline: UK couple chooses India to undergo IVF treatment, calls the healthcare system 'mind-blowing'

primary_source.headline: UK couple chooses India to undergo IVF treatment, calls the healthcare system 'mind-blowing'
primary_source.content:
The in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) process is an emotionally and financially draining process for any couple. Multiple doctor consultations and waiting periods that sometimes last for years can become exhausting for expectant couples. Similar struggles pushed a British couple to visit India to complete their IVF procedure.&nbsp;Instead of going through the long processes in the United Kingdom’s National Health Service (NHS) system, Dave Flew, a photographer, visited India to complete their IVF journey. Calling the Indian healthcare system “simply mind-blowing”, he shared that he and his wife were undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Lucknow.&nbsp;While talking about his experience in an Instagram video, Flew acknowledged that compared to the UK, the Indian system is very efficient, the facilities are incredible, and the staff is quite helpful.&nbsp;“The whole process is a complete revelation,” he exclaimed. The ability to get appointments within that time, and the fact that they could undergo multiple tests within the same premises without having to move around to different locations to complete the process, is quite convenient.&nbsp;        View this post on Instagram            
 Flew was amazed that even the test results took no longer than 15 to 30 minutes. In the UK, test results for X-rays also sometimes take months. Therefore, visiting India and undergoing a hassle-free and fast treatment at a much cheaper cost really amazed him.&nbsp;An IVF cycle in India can cost approximately Rs 2,00,000 to Rs 5,00,000. Meanwhile, depending on the clinic, the entire process can cost around Rs 6,00,000 to Rs 10,00,000, according to sources. The UK NHS system does cover the IVF process, but it is not guaranteed for all. Moreover, free IVF under the NHS reportedly covers only 28 per cent of cycles in the UK. Therefore, many couples prefer travelling to countries like India to undergo a much more convenient and cheaper IVF process.

stories.primary_headline: Can Ken Paxton outrun a trail of scandal to win US Senate seat in ruby-red Texas?

primary_source.headline: Can Ken Paxton outrun a trail of scandal to win US Senate seat in ruby-red Texas?
primary_source.content: The Republican state attorney general appears uniquely ill-chosen as a candidate – but he is a political survivor who could yet frustrate Democratic dreamsDepending how you look at the situation, it is either predictable that Ken Paxton, Texas’s attorney general and Republican candidate for US Senate, is struggling in the polls – or impressive that he is not doing worse. Beloved by hardcore Maga voters and regarded with skepticism by the broader voting public, Paxton is also puzzlingly bland. Recently, Donald Trump told a crowd of supporters that the 63-year-old Paxton “may not dress right, he may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen”. The president was endorsing him.Yet it is Paxton’s ability to attract – and somehow scrape through – scandal that makes him a less charismatic, perhaps, but still kindred spirit of “Teflon Don”: nothing sticks. He has survived state prosecution (on securities-related charges that he settled without admitting guilt), impeachment by the Republican-led Texas legislature (on abuse-of-office charges of which he was later acquitted), and so many controversies that it can be difficult to pin down the most outrageous. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture

primary_source.headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture
primary_source.content: A new Washington DC exhibition examines how Toni Morrison, Maya Angelou and more used the Bard’s work to help tell their own stories“William Shakespeare was a black woman.” In 1985, Maya Angelou spoke these words as part of a keynote speech at a convention in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.There, she spoke of the role poetry played in her transition from muteness as a child and how she fantasized herself triumphantly delivering Portia’s speech from William Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice in front of her entire community at church. Though she never got the chance to perform that rendition, Angelou acknowledged her desire to deliver that rendition as part of a lifelong kinship with Shakespeare, a connection she continued to seek out throughout her life whenever she needed heartening or solace. In her eyes, Shakespeare wrote his emotionally desolate Sonnet 29 “for” her; how else could he have so aptly described the harsh realities of the Black feminine condition? Continue reading...

primary_source.content:
The singer-songwriter gets a lift from U2 and likes to reminisce to Bette Midler, but which cheesy Euro banger does she secretly like?The first song I fell in love with
 
 When I was five or six, my mum wouldn’t let me listen to anything other than Christian gospel. Her friend Jane felt sorry for me and brought me a cassette with Whitney Houston on one side and Cher on the other. My ears couldn’t believe what they were hearing. I Will Always Love You made me think: This is what I’m going to do.The first single I bought
 
 So Young by the Corrs, from Sainsbury’s in Walton Village in Liverpool. I couldn’t really afford music as a kid, so buying a record was a big deal. I’d heard the Corrs on the radio, liked their voices and thought: I’m buying this. Continue reading...

sources.headline: ‘How do we welcome the stranger, with humanity or anger?’ The forgotten Germans who found refuge in Ireland

brief_bullets: A new play revisits the story of Ireland’s 18th-century German refugees, whose experience of prejudice and exclusion resonates with today’s debates over immigration.
In the early 18th century, a few thousand Germans fled religious persecution and near starvation in their homeland and ended up in remote rural Irish villages.

The Irish Palatines, as they were known, were poor, conservative homesteaders who couldn’t speak the language and were the object of suspicion and violence – precursors to the displaced Syrians or Afghans of the past decade.
Their story is told in Refuge, a co-production between Staatstheater Mainz and the Irish company Fishamble.
why_it_matters_bullets: Underscores accelerating climate extremes, increasing long-term operational strain on public infrastructure and utility grids.

primary_source.content: A restored version of his 1983 film My Brother’s Wedding, set in South Central LA, brings Burnett’s vision to a new audienceCharles Burnett had a dilemma. He had agreed to attend the wedding of a co-worker, but the wedding was scheduled for the same day and time as a funeral for a childhood friend.Initially, the film-maker – a landmark chronicler of Black working-class lives – decided he’d go to the funeral. But when he tried to break the news to the co-worker, she was so dejected that he couldn’t go through with it. He tried asking the bride to change the wedding – which was “ridiculous to think of trying to do”, he says decades later – but that didn’t work either. He decided he’d go to both events. primary_source.content: A modern-day prospector promised rural Imperial thousands of jobs and millions in tax revenue – but his plan has set off a firestorm of resistanceSebastian Rucci zoomed in on a map in late 2024, looking closely at a large block of brown earth. The barren plot sandwiched between sprawling alfalfa fields and sleepy desert suburbs was exactly what he’d been searching for – the perfect place to realize his dream of building the largest artificial intelligence datacenter in California.The dusty expanse wasn’t an obvious location. It was in the Sonoran desert, just north of the Mexican border, where temperatures regularly rose past 100F (37.8C). Water was scarce in the once-booming agricultural area, which gets its supply from the beleaguered Colorado River. And then, there was the city of Imperial – population 22,000 – to win over. As controversial datacenter projects have sprung up across the US, residents were naturally skeptical of a new, energy-guzzling neighbor. Continue reading...
